title: HW/SW Co-Design Research Engineer for Manycores - Gem5 / Computer Architecture
description:
À propos de l'offre d'emploi

HW/SW Co-Design Research Engineer for Manycores - Gem5 / Computer Architecture

We're currently on the lookout for newly qualified PhD or Masters graduates or someone with some industry experience, with knowledge in areas such as computing architecture simulations and memory for a global technology giant in France.

A true leader in research, development, and innovation, this global technology powerhouse invests heavily into R&D to make huge technological advancements in various sectors.

In this position, you will be working on hardware/software co design for many-core chips, working on hardware component modelling and integrating into simulation environments and you will also design device drivers and libraries in C.

This is a full-time CDD contract until Summer 2027 based on-site in Paris, France. There is a high possibility of it extending.

REQUIREMENTS
For this HW/SW CoDesign Engineer position, ideal candidates have the following:
- Masters or PhD degree with 0-3 years experience.
- New graduate 2026 is okay.
- Previous experience with RTL / GEM5 would be ideal.
- Knowledge about memory architectures and how they are managed by the OS.
- C or C++ language proficiency.

A referral scheme is available for this role.

KEYWORDS
Consumer Electronics / CPU / Computing Architecture / Memory / CPU / Computer Architecture / Gem5 / Simulations

ai_analysis.summary: Moderate fit: the candidate has real RTL/FPGA design experience, ASIC register work at Arista, and solid Linux kernel/driver and memory-management projects, but has zero exposure to Gem5 or architectural simulation environments, which is the core tool required. Strong C/C++ and systems fundamentals partially offset the lack of research-level computer architecture simulation experience.
resume_tips: Add 'Gem5' and 'computer architecture simulation' explicitly if you have any exposure — currently completely absent from resume, which is a hard requirement keyword for this role.
Reframe the Unicycle CPU project vocabulary to emphasize 'RTL design' and 'hardware modelling' since that's the closest match to the job's RTL/Gem5 requirement.
Quantify the Arista ASIC register work (e.g. number of registers, chips impacted, time saved) to strengthen the hardware/chip infrastructure narrative.
Explicitly mention 'virtual memory' and 'OS memory management' in the RFID Driver and myMalloc project descriptions to match the job's memory architecture requirement.
Add a 'Simulation environments' or 'Verilog/RTL' skill entry, since the job explicitly lists this and it's currently missing as a standalone tag.
Move the ARM/STM32 and RFID driver projects higher in the resume — device driver and C library work is directly named in the job description.
